Daniel explains that her surgeon evaluates the bone healing with X-rays, not the physical therapy clinic.
Daniel: When is your next appointment with the surgeon?
Marta: It's on November 14, 2 weeks before the race.
Daniel: You could start jogging as long as your surgeon authorizes it.
Daniel: The decision about the race is up to your surgeon.
Daniel: With the surgeon's approval, I would send you a written jogging plan with the steps from the clinic's protocol.
Daniel: It would be better to alternate walking with jogging, as long as you don't feel pain the next day.
Daniel: I would recommend jogging on a flat surface at first.
Daniel: You should wear your usual running shoes, because the return to running is not the time to break in new ones.

passage.title: Un día difícil en ortopedia
target: Es lunes en el piso de ortopedia del Hospital San Rafael, y la fisioterapeuta Carmen Ruiz supervisa a la practicante Irene Campos.
Carmen: Irene, explícamelo tú antes de que entremos al cuarto.
Irene explica su razonamiento clínico: Don Julio Pacheco tuvo una cirugía de cadera hace 2 días y hoy debe caminar con andador.
En el cuarto 623, Don Julio dice que se siente mareado, algo que ayer no tenía.
Carmen: Don Julio, siéntese y dígame si el cuarto le da vueltas.
Mientras Carmen lo sostiene, la enfermera encargada, Rosa Medina, mide la presión de pie, y el monitor marca 96/58.
Carmen le explica a Irene que un mareo nuevo con la presión baja es un signo de alarma que siempre se reporta.
Carmen: Si sigue mareado, no lo vamos a levantar hoy.
Carmen hace el reporte telefónico desde la estación de enfermería: Doctor Villalobos, le llamo por un cambio de estado en el 623.
El doctor da una orden verbal: Don Julio no se levanta sin ayuda y Rosa le toma la presión otra vez en 2 horas.
Carmen: Le repito la orden para confirmar que la entendí bien.
Más tarde, Óscar, el hijo de Don Julio, hace una petición: quiere llevar a su papá caminando hasta la cafetería.
Para llegar, tendrían que recorrer un pasillo largo y tomar el elevador, y Don Julio todavía está mareado.
Carmen: Óscar, entiendo que quiera llevarlo, pero hoy no es seguro.
Por la tarde, un paciente casi se cae con la asistente de enfermería Leticia Mora porque la silla no tenía freno.
Carmen hace la revisión del evento con ella en un cuarto privado y le dice: Leticia, cuéntame qué pasó; no busco culpables.
Juntas acuerdan que el equipo revise los frenos antes de cada traslado, y Carmen llena el reporte según la política del hospital.
En la entrega de turno, Carmen le dice al fisioterapeuta de la noche: En resumen, según el doctor Villalobos, hoy no se levanta solo.
native: It is Monday on the orthopedic floor of San Rafael Hospital, and physical therapist Carmen Ruiz is supervising the student intern Irene Campos.
Carmen: Irene, explain it to me before we go into the room.
Irene explains her clinical reasoning: Don Julio Pacheco had hip surgery 2 days ago and today he should walk with a walker.
In room 623, Don Julio says he feels dizzy, something he did not have yesterday.
Carmen: Don Julio, sit down and tell me if the room is spinning.
While Carmen holds him, the charge nurse, Rosa Medina, measures his standing blood pressure, and the monitor reads 96/58.
Carmen explains to Irene that new dizziness with low blood pressure is a warning sign that is always reported.
Carmen: If he is still dizzy, we are not going to get him up today.
Carmen makes the phone report from the nurses' station: Dr. Villalobos, I'm calling about a change in condition in 623.
The doctor gives a verbal order: Don Julio does not get up without help and Rosa checks his blood pressure again in 2 hours.
Carmen: Let me read the order back to confirm I understood it correctly.
Later, Óscar, Don Julio's son, makes a request: he wants to walk his dad to the cafeteria.
To get there, they would have to go down a long hallway and take the elevator, and Don Julio is still dizzy.
Carmen: Óscar, I understand you want to take him, but today it isn't safe.
In the afternoon, a patient almost falls with the nursing aide Leticia Mora because the wheelchair had no brake on.
Carmen does the event debrief with her in a private room and tells her: Leticia, tell me what happened; I'm not looking for someone to blame.
Together they agree that the team will check the brakes before every transfer, and Carmen fills out the report per hospital policy.
At the shift handoff, Carmen tells the night physical therapist: In summary, per Dr. Villalobos, he does not get up alone today.
